summary: Gangzhun is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Qinghai Nationalities University until 1989 and earned a master's degree from Northwest Minzu University under Alak Dorje Rinpoche (1998–2001).

Ganzorig Davaa-Ochir works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an M.Phil in Tibetan Studies at the University of Oslo under Hanna Havnevik (attested 2008) and also studied under traditional teacher Lama Byambaa (attested 2008).
Garab Dorje Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Jigdral Yeshe Dorje and Thinley Norbu Rinpoche.

Garcin de Tassy was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Collège de France under Louis-Mathieu Langlès, Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy, and Jean Daniel Kieffer. He founded the Société Asiatique and held a chair at INALCO (1828–1877).

Gareth Fisher specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He earned a Ph.D. in socio-cultural anthropology from the University of Virginia (1999–2006) and became Assistant Professor of Religion and Anthropology at Syracuse University in 2008.

Gareth Sparham works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at McGill University, the Institute of Buddhist Dialectics, and the University of British Columbia under Ashok Aklujkar (Ph.D. ~1980–1989), later lecturing at the University of Michigan (1999–2009).

Gary A. Tubb is an Indologist and philosopher who earned his doctorate under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1972–1979). He taught at Harvard (~1979–1985) and Columbia (~1999–2007) before joining the University of Chicago (~2007–2023).

Gary D. DeAngelis works in religious studies and Buddhist studies, having studied under mentors including Masatoshi Nagatomi, George Rupp, W. J. Johnson, Herbert Mason, and Muhammad Daud Rahbar. He served at the College of the Holy Cross (attested 2017).

Gary Donnelly works in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Oxford, University of Liverpool, and University of Manchester, and held teaching posts at Liverpool (2016–2020), Manchester (2021), and Liverpool Hope University (2023).
Gary Goh Wee Kian is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Hui-Chieh Loy, Jay L. Garfield, Brook Ziporyn, Christopher Anthony Brown, and Cecilia Lim.

Gary Snyder is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who attended Reed College, Indiana University Bloomington, and UC Berkeley, studying under teachers including Chiura Obata and Shunryu Suzuki. He was a professor at UC Davis (1986–2002).

Gary Urton is an anthropologist and historian who studied at the University of New Mexico and University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Ph.D. ~1974–1979). He served on the faculty at Colgate University (1978–2002) and Harvard University (~2002–2020).

Gaspare Gorresio was an Indologist who studied at the University of Turin, University of Vienna, and under Eugène Burnouf and Stanislas Julien. He held the chair for Sanskrit at Turin (1852) and served as librarian at the Royal Library (1852–1891).

Gaston Courtillier was an Indologist who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi and Louis Finot in 1897. He taught at lycées in Mulhouse and Strasbourg, becoming chargé de conférences for Sanskrit at Strasbourg in 1924.

Gaston Paris was a linguist who studied under Friedrich Christian Diez and at the École des chartes. He held posts at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1869–1903) and the Collège de France (1872–1903).
Gaston Renondeau was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the École Polytechnique from ~1899 to 1901.
Gaton Ngawang Lekpa was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Gauri Viswanathan is an Indologist who studied at the University of Delhi and Columbia University (Ph.D. ~1978–1985). After teaching English at Delhi (~1973–1978), she became a professor and South Asia Institute director at Columbia University (~1989).
Gaurinath Sastri was an Indologist and philosopher. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College and University (~1954–1969) and Vice-Chancellor of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (~1976–1979).
Gaurishankar Hirachand Ojha was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Elphinstone College (~1883–1885) and under Bhagwanlal Indraji (~1885–1888).
